newsitem.title: USA: USTR's Barshefsky confident about Kodak WTO case.
newsitem.headline: USTR's Barshefsky confident about Kodak WTO case.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Monday she was confident the World Trade Organization would rule in favor of the United States in a complaint about Japan's photo film and paper markets.

"We have great confidence in the case that we have brought to the WTO," Barshefsky said at a news conference in Rochester, N.Y., following a tour of Eastman Kodak Co's facility. The news conference was broadcasted to reporters in Washington. Barshefsky was joined by Rep. Louise Slaughter, D-N.Y. and Daniel Carp, Kodak's assistant chief operating officer.

Barshefsky said the WTO will establish a panel on October 16 to hear U.S. allegations that the government of Japan thwarted efforts by Kodak to expand in the Japanese film and photo paper markets. Fuji Photo Film Co Ltd is Kodak's primary competitor in Japan.

The United States is pursuing the Kodak case on three fronts at the WTO. It is challenging what it says are government barriers hindering the distribution and display of Kodak products, barriers to foreign suppliers created by Japan's Large Scale Retail Store Law and restrictive business practices.
